facts.raw_span: A 30-year-old Asian man presented with a 6-month history of recurrent pain localized to the lateral side of his left knee
slight tenderness and swelling over the lateral joint line without other abnormalities
Plain radiographs were unremarkable
routine laboratory tests were within normal limits
MRI demonstrated a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau
the lesion was homogeneous and isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images
the lesion appeared heterogeneous with internal specks on T2-weighted images
the lesion was unremarkable on fat-saturated T2 sequences
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed enhancement confined to the peripheral rim of the mass
no satellite lesions identified

concepts.why: The patient's MRI demonstrated a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau, which is consistent with a chondroblastoma, a rare type of bone tumor.
The lesion's heterogeneous appearance with internal specks on T2-weighted images and its location in the epiphysis are suggestive of a giant cell tumor.

The patient's recurrent joint pain and swelling, combined with the MRI findings of a space-occupying lesion, could be indicative of synovial chondromatosis, a condition characterized by the growth of cartilage nodules in the synovium.
The aggressive nature of the lesion, as evidenced by its invasion of the tibial plateau, raises the possibility of an osteosarcoma, a malignant bone tumor.
The lesion's location in the metaphysis and its heterogeneous appearance on T2-weighted images are consistent with a chondromyxoid fibroma, a rare type of benign bone tumor.

rationales.F06: Homogeneous and isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images may indicate cartilaginous tumors.
rationales.F09: Peripheral rim enhancement on Gadolinium-enhanced MRI is common in several bone tumors.

frontier_selector.rationale: The lesion's appearance on MRI, particularly the enhancement pattern on Gadolinium-enhanced sequences and its location, supports Chondroblastoma, which is known for its epiphyseal location and characteristic rim enhancement.
